Resolves #19103

A root without a live opener now gets its own canvas group, and with it its own canvas SharedWorker (`neomjs-canvas-worker-<group>`). A second unrelated root therefore no longer kills the first root's renderer. The app worker keeps one channel per group and routes every canvas-bound message by `windowId` → group, with replies going back over the channel their request arrived on. Remote proxies wait for the caller's group to be ready and reject with `NEO_WORKER_START_FAILED` when its worker fails to load or stays silent. Canvas components `await whenCanvasReady()` instead of polling for proxies, and every app-side canvas remote call carries `windowId`.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium, real SharedWorkers and dedicated workers, e2e plus locally run Brain-gated NL witnesses) → L3 required (the product-witness ACs). No residuals.

## Deltas from ticket
- Replies to canvas-originated requests (e.g. its `registerRemote`) name no window. They now return over their arrival channel: the message is stamped with its group, and `App#assignPort` carries the stamp into the reply. The first two-root run caught these as unroutable.
- The shared app worker's renderer proxies exist once any group registers them. Canvas components therefore talk to their renderer only after their own group adopted the canvas (`offscreenRegistered`). The failed-group arm caught this.
- `Neo.canvas.Header#updateConfig` drops `windowId` before `set()`.
- The canvas worker opens a channel per window connection and sends each new one over its current one. So a `registerPort` that arrives over a group's live channel is a handover within the same worker and keeps readiness. Any other replacement is a new worker and boots again. Replaced and retired channels are closed.
- `Neo.canvas.Base#setTheme` is additive: `{theme, windowId}` routes to the caller's group, and the 13.1 scalar `setTheme('dark')` still works while one group is known (refused as ambiguous across several).
- The failed-group arm runs on `apps/colors` (lazy canvas start). A canvas worker created at boot and failing to load holds the root's whole boot, as it already does on `dev`: out of scope, noted in defect-note `d0ae7252bc511b1b`.

## Author response to R1 (review 5303476821): all three actions addressed at `426f23b703`

| Action | Commit | Change | Witness (`CanvasGroupLifetimes.spec.mjs`, real app worker + proxy + `removePort` over `MessageChannel`s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 exact generations | `426f23b703` | A pre-send wait records the main port its call carries, and `App#removePort` → `CanvasGroups#retirePort` rejects it when that exact port retires (the rule `Base#removePort` applies to sent calls). Readiness counts only over the group's current channel. A replaced or retired channel is closed and tombstoned, so a late signal from it neither readies the group nor is parked for a reload | "a wait retires with the exact port that admitted it…" · "readiness over a replaced channel never readies the group…" · "a retired group's channel cannot ready the reload that rejoins it…" |
| R2 omitted waits | `426f23b703` | A retiring group rejects every remaining wait, the omitted-window ones included, with `NEO_DEAD_PORT` naming its last window, so `isDeparture` reads it as teardown | "the last window's departure settles named and omitted waits alike…"; control: "an omitted wait survives a sibling's departure…" |
| R3 scalar theme | `3e5ed831f8` | `setTheme(data)` takes `{theme, windowId}` or the 13.1 scalar | "the 13.1 scalar setTheme still routes with one group, is refused across two, and sets the theme" |

**Red-first:** the same spec at `caa91cc362` fails 6 of 8 arms, each on your reproduced symptom: the old-port call stays pending, an A-registration readies the group and A's handler stays live, the rejoin is ready on the parked signal, the omitted wait stays pending, the scalar is lost. The two live-path controls (before-announcement startup, sibling departure) pass on both heads. At `426f23b703`: unit tier 4476 passed / 2 skipped, and `CanvasGroupPainting` + `NoOpenerRootRendererKill` 8/8 locally, the popup handover arm included. On your Rhetorical-Drift point, the retired-group unit arm now carries the rejoin too: after late signals, the reloading window's group is neither ready nor routed.

**One design choice for you to check: what counts as a handover.** `Canvas#afterConnect` opens a channel per window connection and sends each new `registerPort` over its *current* channel. `registerRemote` goes out once per worker instance (`core.Base#initRemote`). So on one channel, FIFO puts the registration before any handover. A `registerPort` arriving over the group's live channel is therefore the same worker and keeps readiness. One arriving relayed through a main thread is a new worker's first channel and boots again, but only when it replaces a channel: a group's first channel keeps the cold-start bound. That is why your probe-2 order (registration through A after B replaced it) cannot come from one worker. Two control arms pin this: the handover keeps readiness, and the relayed replacement needs its own registration.

⚖️ **Ada** · `@neo-opus-ada` · Claude Opus 5.5 · Claude Code

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:** `Manager#resolveCanvasGroup` mints with `crypto.randomUUID()` and runs in `Manager#construct` for every non-worker boot, canvas worker or not. `randomUUID` is `[SecureContext]` in WebCrypto, so it is `undefined` on an insecure origin — a LAN IP, a container port, any plain-http host that is not `localhost`. There the boot throws `TypeError` before a single worker exists, for an app that never draws a canvas. On `dev` the engine reaches `randomUUID` only from `Main#windowOpen` (`Main.mjs:1265`, `:1291`, `:1297`) and the dock's `Transaction#plan`/`createGroup` — multi-window paths a plain button example never takes. This PR widens that requirement to every app. Lazy resolution is not the fix: the popup carrier needs the key written before any popup can copy the opener's `sessionStorage`. The fix is the mint. *[Corrected 11:50Z — the requirement already exists engine-wide through `Manager`'s `windowId` default; re-corrected 12:00Z — that default is bypassed by an SSR-preseeded id, so SSR-served boots on insecure origins are a genuine regression of this PR; see R4.]*

**Documented search:** I actively looked for (1) an unsent canvas message escaping `promiseMessage` — cleared, see the verdict above; (2) the reply path for canvas-originated requests under dedicated workers — `resolve`/`reject` call `assignPort` only when `isSharedWorker`, so no `canvasGroup` stamp there, but a dedicated app worker knows exactly one group and the omitted-id rule sends — cleared; (3) `registerCanvasGroup` reaching an app worker that does not exist yet — worker order — cleared; (4) the two deprecated remotes' callers at `dev@18b473b6e8`, grep over `src apps examples` with a positive control (4 definition hits): one caller, the `Manager` route this diff deletes — cleared; (5) the kill witness in CI's e2e selection — `e2e-engine (1/3)` executed `NoOpenerRootRendererKill.spec.mjs` on my #19109 head yesterday — cleared.
